blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the tax vocabulary sharpens. Effective tax rate, cash tax, deferred tax, permanent difference, temporary difference, tax base, tax credit, tax shield. Each word has a precise meaning, and at the top of the company, using these terms correctly is not optional — it is part of how serious people recognise each other.

What matters at this level is not memorising definitions but understanding the distinctions between words that look similar. The effective tax rate is what the company reports; cash tax is what the company actually pays. The two are often different, and the gap reveals something about how the company's deferred taxes are moving. A board that does not grasp this distinction cannot have an intelligent conversation about its own tax position.

It is the precision of these words that separates a finance leader the board can trust from one the board quietly stops consulting.

items.q: According to the text, why is using tax terms correctly "not optional" at the top of the company?
options: It is part of how serious people recognise each other
It reduces the company's cash tax
It is required by the tax authorities
items.why: "using these terms correctly is not optional — it is part of how serious people recognise each other."

items.q: What distinction does the text draw between effective tax rate and cash tax?
options: The effective tax rate is what the company reports; cash tax is what it actually pays
The effective tax rate is paid; cash tax is reported
Both mean exactly the same thing
Cash tax applies only to foreign subsidiaries
items.why: "The effective tax rate is what the company reports; cash tax is what the company actually pays."

items.q: According to the text, what does the gap between the two figures reveal?
options: How large the company's tax credits are
How the company's deferred taxes are moving
How aggressive the company's auditors are
items.why: "the gap reveals something about how the company's deferred taxes are moving."

items.q: The text suggests that a finance leader who confuses these terms will most likely…
options: be asked to retrain the auditors
be quietly stopped from being consulted by the board
items.why: Inferência: a precisão separa quem o conselho confia de quem o conselho "quietly stops consulting".

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The most valuable skill is reciting textbook definitions of each tax term
Similar-looking terms can carry very different meanings
Precise language builds a board's trust in a finance leader
Memorising definitions matters less than understanding distinctions
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o que importa "is not memorising definitions but understanding the distinctions".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry orientando a nova diretora financeira antes do comitê de auditoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right — before your first audit committee, let's get one distinction absolutely clean, because everything else hangs off it. When someone at that table says "effective tax rate", they mean the number we report in the accounts. When they say "cash tax", they mean what actually left the bank. Do not use them interchangeably. If you do, someone will notice, and you will spend the rest of the meeting rebuilding your credibility.

Here is why the two diverge. A temporary difference reverses over time — you pay later, or you paid earlier, but eventually it evens out. A permanent difference never reverses; it simply is what it is. The deferred tax line is where the temporary ones live. So when the chair asks why our effective rate is twenty-six but the cash we paid implies something lower, the honest answer is usually the deferred taxes, not some clever scheme.

One more thing. Say "incur a liability", "claim an exemption", "apply a deduction" — the collocations matter as much as the nouns. Get the verb wrong and the room hears an amateur, however good your numbers are. Read the notes aloud tonight. I would rather you sound deliberate than fast.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What single distinction does Harry want to get "absolutely clean" first?
options: Effective tax rate versus cash tax
items.why: "let's get one distinction absolutely clean… When someone says 'effective tax rate'… 'cash tax'…"

items.q: According to Harry, how does a temporary difference behave over time?
options: It is always paid in cash immediately
It reverses and eventually evens out
items.why: "A temporary difference reverses over time… eventually it evens out."

items.q: Why does Harry insist on collocations like "incur a liability" and "claim an exemption"?
options: Because the wrong verb makes the room hear an amateur
Because they are easier to pronounce
Because the tax authorities require those exact words
Because they lower the effective tax rate
items.why: "Get the verb wrong and the room hears an amateur, however good your numbers are."

items.q: When the effective rate is 26 but the cash paid implies something lower, what does Harry say the honest explanation usually is?
items.why: "the honest answer is usually the deferred taxes, not some clever scheme."

items.q: What does Harry imply with "I would rather you sound deliberate than fast"?
options: Precision and composure count for more than a quick answer
Speed of delivery matters more than accuracy
She wants the meeting to finish early
items.why: Inferência: ele prioriza credibilidade e precisão sobre rapidez — soar ponderado vale mais do que responder rápido.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our headline number looks high, but the effective tax rate tells a more nuanced story." The effective tax rate is…
options: the tax charge as a proportion of pre-tax profit that the company reports
the tax the company actually pays out in cash
the statutory rate set by the government
the interest saved by carrying debt
items.why: Effective tax rate = alíquota efetiva: o encargo tributário reportado como proporção do lucro antes de impostos.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The rate we report and the ___ we settle in the bank rarely match in any single year."
items.why: Cash tax = imposto efetivamente pago, o que sai do caixa — em contraste com a alíquota reportada.

items.q: "A permanent difference, unlike a temporary one, will…"
options: be recorded only in cash tax
never reverse — it does not even out over time
always create a deferred tax asset
items.why: Permanent difference = diferença permanente: nunca reverte, ao contrário da temporária.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "By carrying debt, the group creates a ___ — the interest is deductible, so its tax bill falls."
items.why: Tax shield = escudo fiscal: a economia de imposto gerada por despesas dedutíveis, como juros.

items.q: "The board's questions turned on a single distinction that most of them had blurred." Here, distinction means…
options: a mark of honour or prestige
a precise difference between two similar concepts
items.why: Distinction, neste contexto, = distinção: a diferença precisa entre dois conceitos parecidos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e collocations que aparecem em comitês de auditoria e reuniões de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The chair still has to sign off on the tax provision before we file." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two committee members pushed back on the effective-rate reconciliation." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The director promised a cleaner tax note but never followed through." She…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto — não cumpriu.

items.q: "Tidying the wording will not move the needle on our cash tax." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We should flag up the permanent difference before the chair spots it." To flag up means to…
options: raise or draw attention to it proactively
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar atenção para algo de forma antecipada.
